method: 24 authored concepts and 40 bounded seeded grammar graphs; every initial result visually reviewed using 11 contact sheets, with corrected Unicode fixture reviewed again. Successful sources compiled three times (original, repeat, comment plus CRLF). Chromium checked actual painted geometry and text bounds. Subjective beauty/clarity scores are 1–5, not automated assertions. Five diagnostic-isolation control variants were rendered and visually reviewed separately; compilation success alone does not make those controls ideal presentations.
limitations: One fixed seed, 5–9 nodes per generated graph; not exhaustive or coverage-guided fuzzing.
Static native SVGs on one Chromium/Linux font environment; this does not establish animated drag quality or cross-platform typography.
Geometry checks sample path interiors and do not prove every possible intersection absent.
Beauty and semantic clarity require human judgment; Fit font size is a heuristic.

findings.title: Recover label placement by expanding unconstrained layouts
findings.evidence: Four unpinned graphs fail with no feasible label position. Every one renders after removing edge captions; the five-consumer fan-out also renders with explicit vertical alignment and an 8g gap.
findings.opportunity: Retry bounded rank/row spacing or outer caption rails before rejecting a graph without conflicting hard constraints. Preserve explicit pins and return a diagnostic if recovery is genuinely impossible.
findings.acceptance: All four unchanged sources render deterministically with readable captions and the existing geometry/leader checks still pass.

findings.title: Keep unconstrained parallel endpoints in consistent lane order
findings.evidence: Three connections between a Client and Server weave even though straight separated lanes fit; the WebSocket caption ends far below the nodes. Opposing feedback and record-slot operations show similar lane exchanges.
findings.opportunity: Coordinate free endpoint ordering across both ends and consider route/caption cost for the bundle. Respect fixed named-port order. Distinguish legitimate crossings in constrained and nonplanar graphs from avoidable crossings.
findings.acceptance: The three unconstrained parallel protocols have noncrossing, separated lanes and nearby unambiguous captions; record slots retain their exact positions.

findings.title: Include fitted text size and viewport shape in presentation quality
findings.evidence: 22 of 58 rendered diagrams have minimum fitted text below 8 px in a 730 by 450 px panel. The eight-stage pipeline is about 15.5:1 with 5.8 px minimum text; the weakest parallel sample is about 4.6 px. These are readability heuristics, not geometry errors.
findings.opportunity: Offer an aspect-aware folded or vertical presentation for long chains, with a readable zoom floor and panning when a full Fit would make text too small. Changing CSS scale alone cannot improve the underlying frame.
findings.acceptance: A standard documentation-width preview can show the eight-stage concept with readable labels and an obvious sequence; explicit positions remain authoritative.

findings.title: Provide width-aware node and caption wrapping
findings.evidence: Long single-line titles stretch rectangles, cylinders and especially diamonds. The explicitly multiline Unicode gateway shows that a compact, readable result is possible.
findings.opportunity: Add an opt-in or bounded automatic line-break policy based on measured glyph widths, with special treatment for diamond geometry and connection captions. Preserve the source label and SVG description.
findings.acceptance: Long service names remain readable in compact bodies without glyph overflow; Unicode graphemes, manual newlines and SQL slots retain correct metrics.

findings.title: Improve sibling grouping and branch centering in fresh layouts
findings.evidence: Equal-role producers are staggered across multiple ranks, and some trees double back around their root or mix sibling depths. The clean tree-4 sample shows a more legible sibling structure.
findings.opportunity: Use stable sibling ordering and subtree centering with crossing/bend penalties after initial ranking. Prefer visible depth when it does not conflict with explicit constraints or an established drag layout.
findings.acceptance: Fresh fan-in and tree layouts make role/depth groups easy to identify and reduce avoidable bends; drag mental-map stability remains unchanged.

findings.title: Clarify the meaning of disjoint shared-scope islands
findings.evidence: All three members share a tint, but the Trusted boundary badge sits above API alone. A viewer can mistake the two other islands for unrelated highlights.
findings.opportunity: Consider a repeated keyed scope badge, a common legend, or a boundary style that explicitly communicates shared membership without including nonmembers. Treat this as a design choice, not a collision defect.
findings.acceptance: A viewer can identify all three trusted members from the static image without accidentally including Browser.

followUp.summary: Fixed the four reported presentations in the engine while preserving their unconstrained input sources. Original measurements and reviews above describe baseline 38f8245.
changes: Long simple paths fold into a compact sequence when unconstrained.
Simple fans group leaves in a column, nest outer and inner routing channels without crossings or shared segments, and put captions on the horizontal leaf branches.
Parallel protocols keep matching lane order and reserve caption clearance, including during dragging and reopening saved pins.
followUp.verification: All 114 Rust tests/doctest pass. Fan regression coverage checks both directions with three through eight leaves for branch crossings, overlapping segments and caption locality. The other regressions cover explicit row overrides, straight protocol lanes and drag/reopen caption clearance. The full seeded audit and browser checks validate the resulting painted layouts.
